Manatee season in Crystal River is the best time of year to swim with manatees. From mid-November through March, hundreds of them leave the cooling Gulf and crowd into the warm springs of Kings Bay. So if you have been waiting for the right moment to book, this guide explains when to come, what the water is like, and how to get the most out of your swim.

## When manatee season in Crystal River starts

The season starts when the Gulf of Mexico cools down. Manatees can't handle cold water for long, so they look for a warm place to wait out the winter. The springs in Kings Bay stay at 72 degrees all year, and that makes them the perfect shelter. As a result, the first big groups usually show up in mid-November.

The peak comes in January and February. On a cold morning, you can find dozens of manatees resting in one spring. Then, as the Gulf warms up again in March, manatee season in Crystal River winds down and they slowly head back out to the river and the coast.

![Manatee season in Crystal River: a mother and calf rest in clear spring water](photo:trip/abc123)

Still, the season isn't a hard line. In fact, a few manatees stay in Kings Bay all year. You will simply see fewer of them in summer, and they move around more.

## Why Kings Bay is the place to be

Kings Bay is fed by more than 70 springs. Because the water comes up from the aquifer, it stays clear and warm even when the air is cold. For that reason, the bay is one of the most important winter homes for manatees in Florida.

Crystal River is also the only place in the United States where you can legally swim with manatees. However, there are strict rules, and we follow them on every trip. You can read more about how the springs shape their habitat in our post on [where manatees live in Kings Bay](/news/manatee-tours-manatee-habitat).

Here is what makes the bay special in winter:

- The springs hold a steady 72 degrees.
- The water is often clear enough to see the bottom.
- Seagrass and other plants give the manatees plenty to eat.
- The shallow water lets you float right at the surface.

## What to expect during manatee season in Crystal River

Most winter mornings start cool and calm. First, we meet at the dock and get everyone into a wetsuit. Next, Capt. Travis goes over the manatee manners on the boat. Then we head out to find a quiet group of manatees.

Once we find them, you slip into the water and float at the surface. Your wetsuit keeps you warm and helps you stay up without effort. Meanwhile, your guide stays right beside your group the whole time.

Manatees are curious animals. Sometimes a young one swims right up to look at you. Other times, a whole group naps on the bottom while you watch from above. Either way, the calmer and quieter the group, the longer they tend to stay.

![A snorkeler floats quietly above a manatee during manatee season in Crystal River](photo:trip/def456)

## Tips for your manatee swim

A little planning goes a long way. These simple tips help you enjoy the trip and protect the animals at the same time.

1. Book a morning tour if you can. The water is usually calmest early in the day.
2. Bring a towel and a dry set of clothes for the ride home.
3. Wear reef-safe sunscreen, even on a cloudy day.
4. Keep your hands to yourself. Touching manatees is not allowed.
5. Move slowly and kick gently, so you don't stir up the bottom.

Also, check the weather before you go. We tour rain or shine, and during manatee season in Crystal River a cold morning often means more manatees in the springs. If you have questions about gear, ages or swimming skills, our [frequently asked questions](/faq) cover the details.

## How to respect the manatees

Manatees are a protected species, and the rules are there for a good reason. We practice passive observation, which means we watch and let the manatees decide how close they come. For example, we never chase, corner or dive down on a resting manatee.

The rules come from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service and the state of Florida. If you want to learn more before your trip, the Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission has a helpful page on [manatee biology and protection](https://myfwc.com/wildlifehabitats/wildlife/manatee/).

![A manatee surfaces for a breath near Three Sisters Springs in Kings Bay](photo:trip/ghi789)

In short, a respectful swim is a better swim. When the group stays calm, the manatees relax and often stay close. That is when the best moments happen, like a calf rolling over to look at you or a big adult drifting past close enough to see every whisker.

## Planning your trip

Manatee season in Crystal River is also the busiest time of year in town, so it pays to plan ahead. Hotels, rentals and boats all fill up, especially around the holidays. Weekends and holidays fill up first. On the other hand, weekday mornings in January are often a little quieter.

Our boat takes six guests at most. That keeps the group small and the experience personal. You can choose a shared tour and join other guests, or book a private tour and have the whole boat to yourself. Either way, every tour includes a wetsuit, snorkel gear and free GoPro photos from your swim.

When you are ready, take a look at [our manatee tours](/tours) and pick the time that suits your group. Then [check open dates](/book) and save your seats. We can't wait to share the water with you this winter.
